clue.text: Be concerned, extremely sedulous — gentle touch

parts.note: to care is to be concerned about something

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, taken here from sedulous

explanation.surface: A diligent person worries, and comforts someone with a soft touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the outer letters of 'sedulous', S and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A caress is a light, affectionate stroke, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Evasive about sea in A Midsummer Night's Dream?

indicators.note: the evasive word goes about, or around, the sea word

parts.note: coy means reluctant to give details, evasive
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Someone is being cagey about a sea that appears in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play is an example of the dramatic genre, hence the question mark marking a definition by example.

clue.text: Tackle puzzle again? Determination!

definitions.meaning: read as ..., to work out a puzzle a second time

explanation.surface: Having another go at a puzzle shows real grit.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve as a noun means steadfast determination; split as re-solve it means work out again.

clue.text: Exchange hands when reversing

indicators.note: the word for hands is read backwards

parts.note: paws is informal for hands

explanation.surface: Hands are swapped over while driving in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to trade one thing for another, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Busy man in charge outside court

indicators.note: the man and in-charge letters sit outside the court abbreviation

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A busy official runs things just outside the courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Hectic describes a period full of frantic activity, so busy is a synonym.

clue.text: No longer quiet, lawful, showing graphic detail

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
licit means permitted by law

explanation.surface: Something once hushed and legal is now out in the open in graphic terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Explicit content shows everything plainly, especially sexual or violent detail.

clue.text: US writer that wrote an immature novel to begin with

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the five words is taken

explanation.surface: An American author who produced a juvenile novel early in his career.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain was the pen name of the American novelist Samuel Clemens.

clue.text: Carry clubs — envoy playing

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of envoy are moved about

explanation.surface: A diplomat lugs a golf bag of clubs while playing a round.
explanation.definitionFit: To convey is to transport or carry from one place to another.

clue.text: Dirt involving leading performer — hot stuff?

indicators.note: the dirt word wraps around, involving, the performer word

parts.note: mud is wet dirt
the star is the lead of a show

explanation.surface: A celebrity is caught up in mud-slinging, which makes them hot property.
explanation.definitionFit: The condiment is pungent and fiery, so it is hot stuff in a literal culinary sense.

clue.text: Daughter, mad at animal — this one?

definitions.text: Daughter, mad at animal — this one?

indicators.note: mad, read as crazy, says the following letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A girl is furious with a dog, perhaps one of the spotty ones.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well: a daughter cross at a dog, wondering whether it is the spotted breed.
explanation.definitionFit: This spotted breed is the kind of animal a child might be cross with, chewing things up.

clue.text: One easily manipulated accepting ultimately inferior seafood

indicators.note: the pawn takes in a letter

parts.note: a pawn is someone used by others

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of inferior

explanation.surface: A pushover settles for second-rate fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This crustacean is a common shellfish eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Husband leaving Indian city food shop

indicators.note: the husband's letter leaves the city's name

parts.note: Delhi is the city in northern India

explanation.surface: A husband walks out of a grocery in an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for delicatessen, a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods.

clue.text: Everyone in Church welcoming a group with common purpose

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: the in-and-church letters welcome a single letter inside

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The whole congregation in church greets a gathering united in purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union of parties for shared aims, matching a united group.

clue.text: Time dish cooked with oatmeal?

definitions.meaning: British slang for a prison sentence, as in doing time
the breakfast dish of oats boiled in milk or water

explanation.surface: Breakfast cooking time for an oatmeal dish.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, doing porridge means serving a prison sentence, which is time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: slang for a jail term and the hot oat breakfast.

clue.text: No team player! Come again, silly!

indicators.note: silly signals the letters are jumbled foolishly

explanation.surface: A coach berates a selfish player: come on, don't be silly!
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obsessed with themselves rarely puts the side first, so a selfish individualist fits.

clue.text: Ring off after tea — feeling of annoyance

indicators.note: the scrambled ring comes after the tea

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are disordered

parts.note: ring is taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: The phone rings off after a cup of tea, which is annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexation at being humiliated or disappointed.

clue.text: Where to learn about politician, American

parts.note: ca, circa, means about
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A learning place for an American politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A university's grounds are the site where students study.

clue.text: Unpleasantly cold country, they say

indicators.note: they say signals a word heard rather than written

parts.note: Chile is a South American country

explanation.surface: People claim a certain country is unpleasantly cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilly means cold enough to be uncomfortable.

clue.text: Minor planet, it soared off course

indicators.note: off course means the letters stray out of order

explanation.surface: A small body in space flew wildly off its path.
explanation.definitionFit: Asteroids are small rocky bodies orbiting the sun, also called minor planets.

clue.text: Manner of walking in theatre advised

indicators.note: the letters lie in the words theatre advised

explanation.surface: Stage direction on how an actor should walk.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's tread is their step or way of placing their feet.

clue.text: Money conflict when pounds go missing

indicators.note: the pounds letter disappears from the conflict word

parts.note: a clash is a conflict
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: A row erupts when someone's pounds vanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash is ready money in coins and notes.

clue.text: Bakery product — good bribe

parts.note: a bun is a small baked roll or cake

explanation.surface: A bakery offers a good bribe in the form of a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: BUNG is British slang for a bribe or illicit payment.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal term for a backhander, money paid to sway someone.

clue.text: Reportedly took legal action against fraud

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard rather than spelt, with a silent first letter

parts.note: sued means took someone to court

explanation.surface: Rumour has it someone sued over a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: The P is silent, so the word sounds just like the past tense of sue.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseud is a pretentious person, an intellectual phoney or fake.

clue.text: Having embraced university, learnt about not taking sides

indicators.note: the scrambled letters embrace another letter
about signals the letters of learnt are turned about

explanation.surface: A student at university has learnt the value of impartiality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LEARNT to NETRAL, and 'Having embraced' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutral party stays impartial, siding with nobody.

clue.text: Source of light capturing dodge regularly used without warning

indicators.note: the light source captures letters inside it

parts.note: the sun is the main source of daylight

indicators.note: regularly picks alternate letters of dodge

explanation.surface: Sunlight catches a trick used routinely, unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly used' takes the odd letters of 'dodge', DDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden means happening unexpectedly, as in all of a sudden, with no warning.

clue.text: Business season not convincing you at the beginning

parts.note: to season timber is to age it

indicators.note: the opening letters of the three words are taken

explanation.surface: A firm finds the season unpersuasive from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'season' is a verb here: wood is seasoned, or aged.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is a firm providing a particular service, a kind of business.
